steps.description:
Defining a virtual boundary around an object or an area is an approach used to simplify the detection of collision, overlapping, intersection, etc.

The diagram below shows some points on a Cartesian coordinate. You will be writing a program to find the left and right boundaries of the points.


Write a program that asks the user to enter a list of point coordinates (x,y). The input ends when user enters 0,0 (not counted as one of the points). It will then call a function to find the left and right boundaries and display the returned results.

You will need to create the function that takes in a list of points and return the minimum x and maximum x values.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 1,1 7.2,5 4,69 0,0

1,1 7.2,5 4,69 -5,12 10,-9 0,0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point (x,y): 1,1 Enter point (x,y): 7.2,5 Enter point (x,y): 4,69 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min x 1.0 max x 7.2

Example 2 Enter point (x,y): 1,1 Enter point (x,y): 7.2,5 Enter point (x,y): 4,69 Enter point (x,y): -5,12 Enter point (x,y): 10,-9 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min x -5.0 max x 10.0

The diagram below shows some points on a Cartesian coordinate. You will be writing a program to find the top and bottom boundaries of the points.


Write a program that asks the user to enter a list of point coordinates (x,y). The input ends when user enters 0,0 (not counted as one of the points). It will then call a function to find the top and bottom boundaries and display the returned results.

You will need to create the function that takes in a list of points and return the minimum y and maximum y values.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 1,1 7.2,5 4,69 0,0

1,1 7.2,5 4,69 -5,12 10,-9 0,0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point (x,y): 1,1 Enter point (x,y): 7.2,5 Enter point (x,y): 4,69 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min y 1.0 max y 69.0

Example 2 Enter point (x,y): 1,1 Enter point (x,y): 7.2,5 Enter point (x,y): 4,69 Enter point (x,y): -5,12 Enter point (x,y): 10,-9 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min y -9.0 max y 69.0

The diagram below shows some points on a Cartesian coordinate. You will be writing a program to find the boundary of the points.


Write a program that asks the user to enter a set of points in the Cartesian coordinate system. The input ends when user enters 0,0 (not counted as one of the points). It will then call a function to find the boundary box and display the returned results.

You will need to create a function that takes in a list of points and compute the boundary box that can contain all the points by returning the following 4 values: minimum x value maximum x value minimum y value maximum y value

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input 1,1 7.2,5 4,69 0,0

5,6 -2,-4.4 -23,9 67,-60 0,0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below: Example 1 Enter point (x,y): 1,1 Enter point (x,y): 7.2,5 Enter point (x,y): 4,69 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min x 1.0 max x 7.2 min y 1.0 max y 69.0

Example 2 Enter point (x,y): 5,6 Enter point (x,y): -2,-4.4 Enter point (x,y): -23,9 Enter point (x,y): 67,-60 Enter point (x,y): 0,0 min x -23.0 max x 67.0 min y -60.0 max y 9.0
steps.answer:
def findBoundaryBox(points):
    min_x = points[0][0]
    max_x = points[0][0]
    min_y = points[0][1]
    max_y = points[0][1]
    
    for p in points:
        if p[0] < min_x:
            min_x = p[0]
        if p[0] > max_x:
            max_x = p[0]
        if p[1] < min_y:
            min_y = p[1]
        if p[1] > max_y:
            max_y = p[1]
            
    return min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y

points = []
while True:
    ans = input("Enter point (x,y): ")
    if ans == "0,0":
        break
    p = [float(ans.split(",")[0]), float(ans.split(",")[1])]
    points.append(p)
    
min_x, max_x, min_y, max_y = findBoundaryBox(points)
print("min x", min_x)
print("max x", max_x)
print("min y", min_y)
print("max y", max_y)
